Actual feedback first. The current source batch (batch-0497cdd238512a92-0, controller.gvs_nmpc@10.0.0, T0 structure, holding_tip_speed_weight 0.05) completed as a finite valid execution (F1992 true) with zero solver errors (F1895) and zero force-bound violation (F1769); tip terminal reach passed (F1887) at 0.00307 m terminal error (F1903) and holding position passed (F1775) at 0.00331 m max error (F1945). Its single binding deficiency is held tip speed: holding max speed 0.03390 m/s (F1986) exceeds the frozen 0.02 m/s limit, so holding_speed_passed is false (F1926), accepted is false (F1777) and status is valid_failure (F1899). This is what makes the choice a control-weight question rather than a reach question, and it is why I do not restart a structural batch.

Consuming the completed controller10 evaluations (all T0 structure, terminal_tip_speed_weight fixed at its 0.1 upper bound, only holding_tip_speed_weight varied) shows held tip speed is strongly non-monotone in the weight: 0.025 -> 0.0555 m/s, 0.0375 -> 0.00882 m/s, 0.04375 -> 0.0339 m/s, 0.05 -> 0.0339 m/s, 0.06875 -> 0.0383 m/s, 0.075 -> 0.0379 m/s (canonical facts f_4bc6b31b14b043e5b0a3, f_d3dfbc5463bdda7e7a58, f_9fa51480f0a3169f3039, f_c7b3206fcf207688e638, f_6c8b65e37484b17ef739, f_c6b31b14b043e5b0a3-equivalent weight rows). Exactly one point is a joint pass: batch-89c582abe35fdd32-1 (execution_id 1b81c75b9ab6495ca529ed77f4395f1e, configuration artifact 07e86f36a965759c54badbabf9232a9425e5a7643389e00b25f8c586ee7ddf81, holding_tip_speed_weight 0.0375) with terminal_error 0.0030958 m (f_e53ab3e4690820e9ed36), holding_max_error 0.0030958 m (f_902215291ed741572c43), holding_max_speed 0.0088152 m/s (f_d3dfbc5463bdda7e7a58), joint_reach_holding_passed true (f_0394d2b4d55321cc9f41), valid_complete_execution true (f_04d9c3d57483f47b1a6f), force_bound_violation_n 0.0 (f_c53cb960ce40610e1d17) and solver_error_count 0 (f_7e2078f37554d9588c0b). So supported speed-weight adaptation does attain joint nominal reach-and-hold on this single nominal case: the frozen question is answered yes, with narrow support, and the pass is NOT attributable to the terminal weight (already at its 0.1 bound).

The candidate-local bounded-endpoint evidence for the other templates (e.g. F523-F594) only places target equilibria as feasible_in_local_model; that is a local affine witness, not a nonlinear certificate, and unavailable points are not physical-infeasibility proofs, so no cross-template structural claim is made.
